Moisten the yufka with the sauce, fold with the filling and arrange on the tray.

İçli köfte (stuffed bulgur shells)
For the shell: 2 cups fine bulgur
250 g lean mince (for the shell)
For the filling: 250 g medium-fat mince
Half a cup walnut kernels
1 dessert spoon black pepper
3 cups sunflower oil for frying
Soak the bulgur in 1 cup lukewarm water and leave for 20 minutes.
For the filling, fry the onion with the mince until the liquid evaporates; add the spices, walnuts and parsley and let it cool.
Knead the bulgur, semolina, lean mince, egg and salt for 15 minutes into a dough that doesn’t stick to your hands.
With wet hands, take a walnut-sized piece and hollow it out with your index finger into a thin shell.
Put 1 dessert spoon of filling inside, close it up and shape with two pointed ends.
Deep-fry in plenty of preheated oil (170 °C) for 4–5 minutes until golden; drain on kitchen paper.
To boil instead, cook in boiling salted water for 5 minutes after they rise to the surface.
Shaped köfte can be frozen on a tray, then bagged and kept for 2 months.
Hot or warm.
2 days in a sealed container; 1 month in the freezer.
Homemade baklava
40 sheets baklava pastry
2 cups finely ground walnuts or pistachios
For the syrup: 3 cups sugar
Juice of half a lemon
For the syrup, boil the sugar and water, simmer for 12 minutes, add the lemon juice and cool completely.
Melt the butter and skim off the foam.
Grease the tray; lay half the sheets, brushing butter between each one.
Spread the walnuts evenly and lay the remaining sheets on top, buttering them the same way.
Cut into baklava pieces with a sharp knife and pour the remaining hot butter over the top.
Bake in a 180 °C oven for 50–60 minutes until golden.
Ladle the cold syrup over the hot baklava; leave to rest for at least 4 hours.
The syrup must be cold and the baklava hot; if both are hot, it turns doughy.
Cold or at room temperature.
3 days in a sealed container in the fridge.
Künefe
250 g kadayıf (shredded pastry)
200 g unsalted künefe cheese or fresh kashar
For the syrup: 1 cup sugar
For the top: 2 tablespoons ground pistachios
Boil the sugar and water for 10 minutes, add lemon and keep warm.
Pull apart the kadayıf by hand into short pieces and toss with melted butter.
Press half the kadayıf into the base of the künefe pan.
Slice the cheese thinly and lay it on, leaving a 1 cm border; cover with the remaining kadayıf and press.
Cook on the hob over a low heat for 6–7 minutes until the bottom is golden, flip with a plate and cook the other side (or bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes).
While hot, pour over the warm syrup, sprinkle with pistachios and serve immediately.
If the cheese is salty, soak it in water for a few hours to remove the salt.
İskender kebab
500 g döner meat or thinly sliced beef tenderloin
4 pide breads
For the sauce: 2 tablespoons butter
3 grated tomatoes
2 tablespoons butter (for sizzling)
Cook the grated tomato, tomato paste and butter for 10 minutes, thin with stock and add salt.
Sauté the meat in a lightly oiled pan over a high heat for 3–4 minutes, without letting it release its juices.
Cube the pide, spread on plates and drizzle with some of the sauce.
Arrange the meat on the pide and pour over the remaining sauce.
Add yogurt on the side; heat the butter until foaming and pour it hot over the meat.
Don’t burn the butter; pour it when it foams and colours slightly.
2 days in a sealed container in the fridge.
Adana kebab
600 g minced lamb (20% fat, hand-chopped with a zırh knife)
2 long red peppers
4 flat skewers
To serve: 4 lavash, 1 onion, 2 tomatoes, 4 green peppers
Chop the pepper very finely and squeeze out the juice.
Knead the mince with the pepper, chilli flakes and salt for 10 minutes until sticky.
Rest in the fridge for 1 hour.
With wet hands, mould the mixture onto the flat skewers 1.5 cm thick, pressing with your fingertips.
Cook over hot charcoal or on a grill for 8–10 minutes, turning.
Serve with lavash and roasted tomatoes and peppers.
If the mince is too lean, the kebab will fall off the skewer.
Etli ekmek (Konya meat flatbread)
For the dough: 4 cups flour
1 packet dried yeast
For the topping: 400 g mince
Salt, black pepper, chilli flakes (1 dessert spoon salt)
Knead the flour, yeast, salt and water and leave to rise for 45 minutes.
Chop the onion, tomato, pepper and parsley very finely; knead well with the mince, paste and spices.
Divide the dough into 6 and roll out into thin, long strips.
Spread the topping thinly and evenly over the dough, pressing it right to the edges.
Bake in a 230 °C oven on a stone or upturned tray for 10–12 minutes.
Slice and serve hot.
Konya style is rolled very thin; it cooks quickly because the topping is spread thinly.
